findings.title: RSU lots N1, N3, N4 computed with zero basis despite Corvane supplement; 47,620 of gain overstated and RSU income double counted
findings.description: R-8949-LOT says broker basis is used unless a supplemental statement for the same lot is matched. The engine matched the D11 supplement for the ESPP lot (F8949.A.N2 cites ev-0072) but not for the three RSU lots. D28 page 3 reports basis 'not reported' for N1/N3/N4 (ev-0498, ev-0516, ev-0525 read as blank, value 0.0), and D11 page 2 gives adjusted basis RSU-2502 19,100.00 (ev-0066), RSU-2505 19,100.00 (ev-0068), RSU-2308 9,420.00 (ev-0070), with matching acquisition dates and share counts (400/400/300 at vest FMV 47.75/47.75/31.40). F8949.B.N1 = 19,240 (should be 140), F8949.B.N3 = 18,480 (should be -620), F8949.E.N4 = 15,300 (should be 5,880). The 2025 vest income 38,200 is already in D08 box 1 (box 14 RSU 38,200), so it is taxed twice. Flows to F8949.B.total 37,720, SchD.2, F8949.E.total 15,300, SchD.9, SchD.7/15/16, F1040.7, F8960, F6251.1 and SchCA540NR.7.E (N1 and N3 were sold during California residency).
findings.expected: N1 gain 140 (19,240 - 19,100); N3 loss -620 (18,480 - 19,100); N4 gain 5,880 (15,300 - 9,420); Box B total -480; Box E total 5,880; adjustment code B on each lot
findings.actual: N1 19,240; N3 18,480; N4 15,300 (basis 0.00 on each); Box B total 37,720; Box E total 15,300
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Federal overstatement about 15,536 (ST 38,200 x 0.348 = 13,294; LT 9,420 x 0.238 = 2,242); California about 2,445 on the two CA-period sales (38,200 x 0.064) plus about 320 on N4; AMT and NIIT also move. Change exceeds the firm's 1,000 partner sign-off threshold.

findings.title: Self-employed health insurance deducted (14,400) although client states Erik was eligible for spouse's employer coverage all year
findings.description: Sch1.17 = 14,400 (ev-0484, D25 individual PPO plan). qa-25: 'Yes - both of Ngozi's employers offer family coverage, but Erik kept his own individual plan'. The 2024 return allowed no SEHI for the same reason (py:/return_2024/notes/Sch1.17: covered on Ngozi's employer plan). Engine rule R-SEHI only applies the income limitation (business income minus half SE tax and SEP) and has no eligibility test, so it deducted the full premiums with no diagnostic. The deduction also reduces F8995.2.1 QBI (81,854 - 5,783 - 15,214 - 14,400 = 46,457), so removing it raises QBI by 14,400 (deduction +2,880) and SchCA540NR.26.D/E. Reviewer/partner decision required; firm rule says tax effect over 1,000 needs partner sign-off.
findings.expected: Sch1.17 = 0 (or only months without employer-plan eligibility), consistent with 2024 treatment and qa-25; premiums remain non-deductible personal (not on Schedule C either)
findings.actual: Sch1.17 = 14,400; engine rule R-SEHI performed no eligibility check
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Approx. +4,464 federal and +605 California (14,400 x 0.31 / 0.042) if fully disallowed, partly offset by a larger QBI deduction (~+2,880 deduction)
findings.proposed_check: sehi_eligibility_gate: if any questionnaire answer indicates eligibility for an employer-subsidized plan (taxpayer or spouse) for a month, block SEHI for that month and compare to prior-year treatment; require a documented judgment with authority.

findings.title: SEP contribution 18,000 exceeds the deductible limit; excess not flagged and limit will shrink after corrections
findings.description: D26 (ev-0485) confirms 18,000 deposited 2026-04-10 for TY2025, matching qa-26 plan. Sch1.16 correctly limits the deduction to 20% x (81,854 - 5,783) = 15,214 per R-SEP-LIMIT, leaving a 2,786 nondeductible excess contribution that no diagnostic surfaces (client needs to withdraw/recharacterize or carry it). If the gross receipts, mileage, Spotify and phone/internet corrections are made (net profit ~73,568, half SE tax ~5,197), the limit falls to ~13,674 and the excess grows to ~4,326. Note v1 and v2 (2026-03-04, 2026-03-19) deducted 15,214 citing qa-26 (a planned contribution) before any contribution existed; D26 first appears in v3 documents_used. The extension payment (timeline extension-2026-04-14) was estimated from v2 with that deduction assumed.
findings.expected: Deduction = min(contribution, 20% x (net profit - half SE tax)) recomputed on corrected profit (~13,674), with the excess (~4,326; at least 2,786 today) routed to the client for correction
findings.actual: Sch1.16 = 15,214 on engine profit; excess 2,786 silent; v1/v2 relied on a planned, unmade contribution
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Each 1,000 of lost SEP deduction ~ +310 federal / +42 California; excess-contribution penalty exposure outside the return
findings.proposed_check: sep_excess_and_timing: flag when contribution document amount > R-SEP-LIMIT result; flag any retirement deduction whose only source is a questionnaire 'plan' answer; recompute limit whenever SchC.31 changes.

findings.title: Home office: Sacramento room 220 sq ft vs 300 sq ft claimed in 2024 for the same house; averaging method and two-home treatment need a decision
findings.description: D24 (ev-0481) measures the Sacramento rental's studio at 11 x 20 = 220 sq ft; the 2024 return used 300 sq ft (py:/return_2024/lines/SchC.30 = 1,500) for the same house, and the prior preparer left 'Home office 300 sq ft (2 rooms combined?) - client to confirm' open (py:/prior_preparer_workpaper). Either 2024 was overstated or 2025 is understated. Engine SchC.30 = average 240 x 5 = 1,200 (R-HOME-OFFICE-SIMPLIFIED, average monthly sq ft). 240 equals (220 x 6 + 260 x 6)/12 only if July is assigned to Austin (occupied 16 days); if July is Sacramento it is 236.7 -> 1,183; day-weighted (195/170) gives 238.6. Separately, two homes were used (Sacramento rented to 07/14, Austin owned from 07/16) and the Austin house is owned, so an actual-expense method for Austin is a reviewer judgment the engine never offered. Engine diagnostic HOME_OFFICE_AREA_CHANGE is info-level only.
findings.expected: Confirmed square footage for both homes with a documented month-assignment convention (240 or 236.7 avg) and a recorded decision on method for the owned Austin home; explanation of the 300 -> 220 change for the same Sacramento house
findings.actual: SchC.30 = 1,200 from a simple average of 220 and 260; 2024 300 sq ft unresolved
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Low on the simplified method (±17 to ±300 deduction); potentially larger if actual expenses are used for the owned Austin home
findings.proposed_check: home_office_py_consistency: compare current-year sq ft per address with prior-year sq ft for the same address; flag changes > 10%; recompute monthly average with an explicit month-assignment rule and show both variants.

findings.title: California: Section 179 election on the 38,000 equipment saves 1,050 CA tax with no federal change (what_if)
findings.description: F4562-C.14 = 38,000 100% special depreciation (R-EQUIPMENT-METHOD default for property acquired after 2025-01-19; D22 invoice 03/14/2025, installed 03/21/2025). California (R-CA-BUSINESS) disallows bonus and caps section 179 at 25,000, producing a 30,400 CA addition (SchCA540NR.12.C) and CA depreciation of only 7,600. what_if.equipment_section179 shows electing section 179 instead: federal total tax unchanged (0), California total tax -1,050 (CA addition 30,400 -> 10,400; FTB3885A per-asset 2,840/3,260/1,500 -> 10,314/11,839/5,447). what_if.equipment_no_bonus (regular MACRS) would cost +10,245 federal. The engine took the default without surfacing the cost-free CA-favorable election; partner sign-off needed (effect > 1,000).
findings.expected: Documented method election; what_if indicates section 179 is weakly dominant (0 federal, -1,050 CA)
findings.actual: Default 100% special depreciation; CA addition 30,400
findings.estimated_tax_effect: -1,050 California if section 179 elected; federal 0
findings.proposed_check: method_election_dominance: for each elective method, compare what_if results across jurisdictions and flag alternatives that are at least as good federally and better in a state.

findings.title: Mileage log substantiation anomalies (same-day multi-trip totals, inconsistent distances to the same destination)

findings.title: RSU lots N1, N3, N4 carried at zero basis although the Corvane supplemental statement (D11) reports adjusted basis of 19,100 / 19,100 / 9,420
findings.description: Northlake reports the three RSU lots as noncovered with basis 'not reported'. Rule R-8949-LOT says broker basis is used 'unless a supplemental statement for the same lot is matched'. D11 page 2 lists RSU-2502 (400 sh acq 02/15/2025, basis 19,100), RSU-2505 (400 sh acq 05/15/2025, basis 19,100) and RSU-2308 (300 sh acq 08/15/2023, basis 9,420), matching N1/N3/N4 exactly by quantity and acquisition date. The engine matched the ESPP lot from the same statement (F8949.A.N2 cites ev-0072, adjustment B -675) but not the RSU lots, so F8949.B.N1 = 19,240, F8949.B.N3 = 18,480, F8949.E.N4 = 15,300 are full proceeds. W-2 box 14 RSU 38,200 (ev-0027) equals the two 2025 vests (19,100 + 19,100), confirming the income was already taxed as wages. Gain overstated by 47,620 (38,200 short-term in Box B, 9,420 long-term in Box E), flowing to SchD.2, SchD.9, SchD.7, SchD.15, SchD.16, F1040.7, F8960.5a and, because N1/N3 were sold while CA resident, to SchCA540NR.7.E. No diagnostic was raised (the engine did flag the analogous zero-basis crypto lot C6).
findings.expected: N1 gain 19,240 - 19,100 = 140; N3 gain 18,480 - 19,100 = -620; N4 gain 15,300 - 9,420 = 5,880 (adjustment code B on each). Box B total -480; Box E total 5,880.
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Federal about -15,536 (38,200 x 0.348 + 9,420 x 0.238, NIIT included); California about -1,299 to -2,445 (38,200 CA-source x 0.034 stcg rate, or x 0.064 ca_source_income rate). Tax is overstated.
findings.proposed_check: noncovered_basis_supplement_match: for every 1099-B lot with basis not reported / 0, search stock-plan supplements and W-2 box 12/14 for a lot with the same quantity and acquisition date and require a basis adjustment or an explicit reviewer decision.

findings.title: Blank 'basis (not reported)' read as 0.00 money with 0.98 confidence on three RSU lots
findings.description: ev-0498, ev-0516 and ev-0525 have value 0.0, value_type money, text_as_read '' and confidence 0.98. The page prints 'basis (not reported)'. A missing value was encoded as a confident zero, which is what let the engine compute full proceeds as gain. The same pattern for the covered flag (text_as_read '' -> False) is harmless, but a money field should be null with a 'not reported' marker, not zero. This is the root cause of the RSU finding; its tax effect is counted there.
findings.expected: value null / flag 'basis not reported', or low confidence, for lots whose printed basis is '(not reported)'.
findings.actual: value 0.0 (money), text_as_read '', confidence 0.98.
findings.estimated_tax_effect: See RSU finding (about 15,536 federal).
findings.proposed_check: empty_read_nonzero_confidence: flag any money value whose text_as_read is empty but whose value is 0 with confidence > 0.5; treat as missing, not zero.

findings.title: California-source capital gain (SchCA540NR.7.E 55,174) includes 11,334 of the S corporation excess-distribution gain prorated by days, and 38,200 of overstated RSU gain

findings.title: Sparbanken interest converted at the 2024 average rate (10.56) instead of the 2025 average (9.86)
findings.description: SchB.1.6 converts SEK 18,450.00 (ev-0960) using ref:fx.SEK.2024_average = 10.56, producing 1,747. The same parameter set carries 2025_average 9.86 (and 2025_year_end 9.71). 18,450 / 9.86 = 1,871 (or 1,900 at the year-end rate). The 10.56 figure is the rate the prior preparer used on the 2024 return (D06 p4, 'SEK 3,700 at 10.56'), so the engine appears to have carried the prior-year rate forward. The wrong year is printed in the line label itself ('at 10.56 SEK/USD') and persisted unchanged through v1, v2 and v3 with no diagnostic. Arithmetic is internally consistent (18,450/10.56 = 1,747.2), so this is a parameter-selection error, not a rounding error. Flows to SchB.2, SchB.4, F1040.2b, SchCA540NR.2.A/2.D/2.E.
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Interest understated by 124: federal about +43 (124 x 0.348); California about +4 to +9 (124 x 195/365 x 0.064, or 124 x 0.069). Small in dollars, but a wrong-year exchange rate printed on the face of Schedule B.

findings.expected: Either an Arizona tax amount paid on Erik's behalf with a Schedule S computation, or documentation that no AZ tax was attributable to him
findings.actual: No AZ amount in any document; ScheduleS.credit = 844 (Oregon only)
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Small: at most CA tax on ~1,212 of income (~0.093 x 1,212 = ~113)
findings.proposed_check: composite_tax_amount_present: when a K-1 or state supplement mentions a composite/withholding payment for the partner, require an amount field; if absent, open a third-party question and block the Schedule S line from being marked verified.

findings.title: Oregon composite tax 1,580 paid April 2026 is counted as a 2025 distribution (inside box 16D 42,000) and drives the 2025 Schedule S credit
findings.description: D39 p2: 'Oregon tax paid on your behalf 1,580 (paid with the composite return in April 2026; included in box 16D distributions)'. The engine used 42,000 as 2025 distributions (F7203.6) and 1,580 x 195/365 = 844 as the 2025 Schedule S credit. Preparer must decide whether the K-1 presentation is accepted as-is (42,000 reduces 2025 basis; credit claimed for 2025 even though the payment date is 2026) and whether the 1,580 belongs on a 2026 SALT schedule. It was correctly excluded from SchA.5a (R-SALT-INCOME: payments dated in 2025 only).
findings.expected: Documented decision on treatment of the 1,580 (distribution year; credit year; SALT year)
findings.actual: Engine silently accepts 42,000 and credits 844 with no note
findings.estimated_tax_effect: If 1,580 were excluded from 2025 distributions: gain -1,580 x 0.238 = ~-376 federal; Schedule S credit 844 at stake for CA
findings.proposed_check: k1_statement_date_scan: parse K-1 statement text for payment dates outside the tax year and route them to a judgment item linked to the affected lines.

findings.title: Ridgeline K-1 received 2026-06-22, after the internal review deadline and the extension; three versions of the pass-through picture
findings.description: qa-13 and msg-01/msg-04 warned the K-1 would arrive in June. v1 (2026-03-04) and v2 (2026-03-19) carried diagnostic K1_EXPECTED_NOT_RECEIVED; the extension payment (2026-04-14, from v2) excluded it. v3 (2026-06-23) first lists D37/D38 in documents_used and changes_from_previous shows the expected lines: SchE.28B +8,400, SchB.1.8 +120, SchD.12 +1,350, Sch3.1 186->396 (+210 box 21), SchE.32 18,400->26,800, F8582.3a and F8582.4 +8,400, SchCA540NR.17.E -21,658 adjusted by +5,348. All reconcile to ev-0964/0965/0966/0968. Box 19A distributions 6,000 (ev-0967) appear on no line (not taxable while under capital account), and carryovers_out.ridgeline_capital_account_end became 63,660.
findings.expected: Late K-1 tracked as an open item from qa-13 onward; its tax effect included in the extension estimate
findings.actual: Extension estimate excluded ~2,750 of federal tax from this K-1 (8,400 x 0.31 + 120 x 0.348 + 1,350 x 0.238 - 210); v3 balance due 4,220 after 36,000 paid
findings.estimated_tax_effect: ~2,750 federal added at v3; penalty exposure on the shortfall
findings.proposed_check: expected_document_tracker: create an expected-document item from questionnaire answers (qa-13) and prior-year K-1s; show which version first used each document and the delta it caused.

findings.title: Ridgeline outside basis never computed; 6,000 distribution tested against nothing
findings.description: py:/basis_records/partnership_ridgeline/0 outside_basis is null ('never computed'). The engine carries only the capital account (63,660) and raised no diagnostic. Box 19A distributions 6,000 are not on any line. The capital account roll on D37 is internally consistent (60,000 + 9,870 - 6,000 - 210 = 63,660), so no gain is indicated, but the workpaper should record that the test was done against the capital account, not outside basis.
findings.expected: Outside basis record started (capital account plus share of liabilities) or an explicit note that capital account is used as a proxy
findings.actual: Null outside basis; no line, no diagnostic for the 6,000 distribution
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None expected (6,000 << 63,660)
findings.proposed_check: partnership_distribution_vs_basis: compare K-1 distributions to the best available basis figure and record which figure was used.

findings.title: Provenance error: CA share percentage (ev-0971) attached to the CA depreciation subtraction line instead of the CA-amount line
findings.description: In v3 SchCA540NR.17.B (CA subtractions, value 484, unchanged from v1) lists ev-0971 (Ridgeline CA share 22%) as a source. The 22% is used only in 17.E (value changed -21,658 -> -16,310; delta 5,348 = 8,400 x 195/365 + 8,400 x 0.22 x 170/365 = 5,349). The arithmetic is right; the citation on 17.B is wrong and would mislead an examiner tracing the depreciation adjustment.
findings.expected: 17.B sources = [asset:SAC-APPL]; 17.E sources include ev-0971
findings.actual: 17.B sources = [asset:SAC-APPL, ev-0971]
findings.proposed_check: source_relevance_check: a source cited on a line whose value did not change when that source was added is flagged as a misattributed citation.

findings.title: Excess-distribution lot carries an unsourced acquisition date (2018-12-20)
findings.description: F8949.F.SCORP label states 'acquired 2018-12-20, sold 2025-12-31' with sources [] and inputs [F7203.excess]. Nothing in household, prior_years or documents gives the date Erik acquired the Woodworks shares. Long-term treatment (0.238 rate) depends on it.
findings.expected: Acquisition date sourced to a document or client answer
findings.actual: Date hard-coded with no source
findings.estimated_tax_effect: If short-term instead: 21,215 x (0.348 - 0.238) = ~2,334 federal
findings.proposed_check: unsourced_literal_check: any date or amount appearing in a line label that is not in inputs or sources is flagged.

findings.title: K-1 identity fields cannot be verified: no TIN printed on D37, D39 or D40; D37 prints no ownership percentage
findings.description: The three K-1 pages name 'Erik Lindqvist' but print no SSN, so the household:erik SSN 666-52-9134 cannot be agreed to the documents. Ownership 20% agrees across D39 (ev-0978), D40 (ev-0986) and qa-12. D37 shows no profit/loss/capital percentage, so the 2024-to-2025 ownership comparison for Ridgeline is impossible; only the capital account (60,000 = py 2024 ending) ties.
findings.expected: Partner/shareholder TIN and ownership percentages on every K-1
findings.actual: No TIN on any K-1 page; no percentage on D37
findings.proposed_check: k1_identity_match: require TIN last-4 and ownership % fields on K-1 extraction; compare to household and prior-year K-1; flag when absent.

findings.title: Photo-sourced extraction (D40) reports 0.99 confidence identical to native PDFs
findings.description: D40 is a phone photo (IMG_5190.jpg) uploaded by the client. Its four values match the printed_content exactly, but the confidence of 0.99 is indistinguishable from PDF-sourced reads; the pipeline's confidence does not reflect source quality. Since these values set the opening basis (F7203.1), the workpaper should force source-document agreement rather than trust the score.
findings.expected: Lower or source-adjusted confidence for photographed documents, or a mandatory agreed_to_source_document step
findings.actual: 0.99 on all four values
findings.proposed_check: photo_source_verification: for documents with image file types, require agreed_to_source_document verification regardless of confidence.

findings.title: Prior-year: 2024 return filed without a Form 7203 although distributions (30,000) exceeded K-1 income (16,900) and basis was unknown
findings.description: D06 contains no Form 7203 lines (return_2024.lines has none) and D07 p2/p5 record 'assumed basis sufficient'. With D40 now in hand the reconstruction is: 2023 ending 21,300 + 14,100 - 20,000 = 15,400; 2024 ending 15,400 + 16,900 - 30,000 = 2,300. The prior preparer's assumption therefore holds (no 2024 excess), but basis_records still show 2023 and 2024 ending as null and should be updated to 15,400 and 2,300.
findings.expected: basis_records 2023 ending 15,400; 2024 ending 2,300; prior-preparer open item 'Obtain 2023 Woodworks K-1' closed
findings.actual: Both years null; open item not marked resolved anywhere
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None for 2024 (basis was sufficient)
findings.proposed_check: basis_record_backfill: when a gap-filling document arrives, recompute and store each intermediate year's ending basis and close the matching prior-preparer open item.

findings.title: F8582 classification and input hygiene for the Ridgeline rental income and line 1a
findings.description: Ridgeline box 2 'net rental real estate income' is placed on F8582.3a (other passive activities) via SchE.32 rather than in the rental activities section (1a). F8582.1a inputs list F4797.9 and SchE.21B, yet its value 105,040 equals F4797.9 alone (SchE.21B is a loss and already in 1b). Net result (F8582.4 = 105,040 - 22,480 - 16,150 + 26,800 = 93,210; all losses allowed) is unaffected.
findings.expected: Rental-type K-1 income grouped with rental activities; inputs limited to lines actually combined
findings.actual: Rental K-1 income on 3a; 1a cites a loss line it does not use
findings.proposed_check: input_contribution_check: for R-8582/R-SUM lines, verify each listed input contributes to the value; flag inputs that do not.

findings.title: Prior-year variance: Woodworks distributions up 40% (30,000 -> 42,000); excess-distribution gain new (0 -> 21,215); no engine variance diagnostic
findings.description: Firm variance_review flags changes over 10% and 1,000 vs prior year. Woodworks distributions rose 12,000 (40%); the capital gain from excess distributions is new; Ridgeline box 2 7,900 -> 8,400 (6%) and Woodworks box 1 16,900 -> 18,400 (9%) are under threshold. The engine produced no variance diagnostic for the distribution jump or for the new 21,215 gain.
findings.expected: Variance items for F7203.6 and F7203.excess requiring explanation
findings.actual: None generated
findings.proposed_check: prior_year_variance: compare each K-1 box and F7203 line to the prior-year figure; raise an explanation item when both thresholds are exceeded or a line is new.

area: Retirement, backdoor Roth, HSA (D41-D45, D26 SEP line, F8606, F8889, Sch1.13/.16, SchCA540NR HSA add-back)
area_notes: Documents: D41 1099-R Northlake IRA (Ngozi; 4 ev: ev-0987 gross 14,026, ev-0988 2b not determined, ev-0989 code 2, ev-0990 IRA box). D42 Form 5498 for TY2024 (received 2026-02-15; ev-0991 box1 7,000, ev-0992 contribution date 2025-02-12; box 5 FMV 12/31/2024 0.00 printed but not extracted). D43 Form 5498 for TY2025 (received 2026-05-29, used first in v3; ev-0993 box1 7,000, ev-0994 box5 FMV 0; box 3 Roth conversion 14,026 printed but NOT extracted). D44 1099-SA (ev-0995 2,150, ev-0996 code 1). D45 5498-SA (ev-0997 box2 6,000 'all employer, through payroll'; box 5 FMV 14,820 and 'family HDHP' printed, not extracted). D26 SEP confirmation (ev-0485 18,000, ev-0486 deposited 2026-04-10, received 2026-04-10, used first in v3). W-2 code W: D08 Corvane ev-0024 2,500; D09 Halvorsen ev-0043 3,500; D10 is a duplicate photo of D09 with its own ev-0060 3,500 (engine counted once). D73 Halvorsen paystub 07/18/2025 shows HSA (cafeteria) YTD 0.00 as of 07/15/2025, i.e. all 3,500 Halvorsen HSA was contributed after the 2025-07-15 move to TX. Every extracted value in the area matches printed_content (values and text_as_read, all confidence 0.99); the planted problems here are omissions, client-vs-document conflicts and sourcing, not misreads. Return lines (identical values v1-v3): F8606.1 7,000; .2 7,000 (py:/return_2024/lines/F8606.14, ev-0991); .3 14,000; .5 14,000; .6 0; .8 14,026; .9 14,026; .10 0.99815; .11 14,000; .13 14,000; .14 0; .16 14,026; .17 14,000; .18 26; F1040.4a 14,026; 4b 26; no Sch1.20 IRA deduction line (correct for nondeductible); F8889.3 8,550 (ref:param.hsa_family_limit), .9 6,000, .13 0, .14a 2,150, .15 2,150, .16 0; Sch1.13 0; Sch1.16 SEP 15,214 = 20% x (SchC.31 81,854 - SchSE.13 5,783) with 18,000 contributed; SchCA540NR.1.C +6,000 HSA add-back, 1.E 218,400 (= sum of box 16), 4.E 26 (both conversions 02/20 and 04/02/2025 fall in the CA residency period, consistent with R-CA-IRA-SOURCE). Sources changed between versions: F8606.1 and F8606.6 cited qa-31 in v1/v2 and ev-0993/ev-0994 in v3; Sch1.16 cited qa-26 (an intention) in v1/v2 and ev-0485 in v3. v3 carryovers_out: ira_nondeductible_basis_ngozi 0 and sep_contribution_not_deductible_for_2025 2,786, but no diagnostic mentions either. Prior year: 2024 return (D06 p10, ev-2991..2993) F8606.1/.3/.14 = 7,000; py:/basis_records/ira_nondeductible_basis_ngozi 7,000; prior preparer open item 'Confirm 2024 Form 5498' (D07 p3) is now satisfied by D42. 2024 CA Schedule CA HSA addition was 2,400 (D06 p12). Cross-area: D09 box 16 (111,300) equals all Halvorsen wages plus HSA although the printed note says CA was the work state only through 09/30 and the client moved 07/15 (qa-45, D73) - wages/California area owns that, but it drives the HSA add-back sourcing finding below.

findings.title: Client says no prior IRA basis; 2024 Form 8606 and 2024 Form 5498 show 7,000
findings.description: qa-31 (Ngozi, 2026-01-20): 'Prior basis: none that I know of - we started doing this in 2025.' D42 (Form 5498 for 2024, received 2026-02-15) shows a 7,000 contribution for tax year 2024 made 02/12/2025, and the 2024 return (D06 p10, ev-2991/ev-2993) filed Form 8606 with line 14 basis 7,000; D07 p1/p6 and py:/basis_records/ira_nondeductible_basis_ngozi agree. The engine correctly used 7,000 on F8606.2, but the workpaper must record that the client's answer was overridden by documents, and the client needs to understand the basis so the 2026 Form 8606 is right. A reviewer who 'corrected' to the client's answer would make the conversion taxable by 7,000.
findings.expected: Prior basis 7,000 (2024 Form 8606 line 14)
findings.actual: Client answer: none. Return: 7,000 (documents win)
findings.estimated_tax_effect: If the client's answer were followed: taxable conversion 7,026 instead of 26 -> about +2,170 federal (7,000 x 0.31) and +693 CA (7,000 x 0.099). Current return: no change.
findings.proposed_check: client_answer_vs_document: when a questionnaire answer and a document/prior-year line disagree on the same fact, open a conflict item that records which source the return used and why.

findings.title: Client reports converting 7,000; Form 1099-R shows 14,026 in two conversions
findings.description: qa-31: 'Ngozi put 7,000 in for 2025 and converted it.' D41 shows two conversions, 02/20/2025 7,010 and 04/02/2025 7,016, total 14,026 (ev-0987), and D43 box 3 prints Roth conversion 14,026. The first conversion is the 2024 contribution made 02/12/2025 (D42). The return follows the 1099-R (F8606.8 and F1040.4a 14,026). The conflict should be documented and the client told that the 2025 return reports 14,026 of conversions.
findings.actual: Client answer 7,000; return 14,026
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None on the current return (engine used the 1099-R). Following the client would understate F1040.4a by 7,026 and mis-state basis.
findings.proposed_check: conversion_amount_three_way: 1099-R box 1 = 5498 box 3 = sum of dated conversions on the 1099-R = client-reported conversion; flag any leg that disagrees.

findings.title: D43 Form 5498 box 3 (Roth conversion 14,026) printed but not extracted
findings.description: D43 printed_content includes 'Box 3 Roth conversion amount (to Roth IRA ending 2291) 14,026.00' but extraction produced only ev-0993 (box 1) and ev-0994 (box 5). F8606.8 therefore rests on the 1099-R alone (ev-0987) with no corroborating 5498 value, and the one document that would independently confirm the conversion total is silently incomplete. Same pattern on D42 (box 5 FMV 0.00 not extracted) and D45 (box 5 FMV 14,820 and 'family HDHP' not extracted) - the HDHP coverage type that drives F8889.3 is cited to ev-0997 (a dollar amount), not to any extracted coverage field.
findings.expected: Extracted values for D43 box 3 = 14,026; D42 box 5 = 0; D45 box 5 = 14,820 and coverage = family
findings.actual: Not extracted (extraction.status 'extracted', values 2 / 2 / 1)
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None directly; loss of corroboration.
findings.proposed_check: printed_fields_not_extracted: parse box labels in printed_content and list every box with a printed value that has no extracted_value on that page.

findings.title: CA HSA add-back sources all 6,000 to California although 3,500 was contributed after the move to Texas
findings.description: SchCA540NR.1.C adds 6,000 (ev-0024 2,500 Corvane + ev-0043 3,500 Halvorsen) under R-CA-WAGES, and 1.E (California amount) is 218,400, the full federal wages plus the full add-back, taken from box 16 of both W-2s (ev-0030, ev-0047). The Halvorsen paystub D73 shows HSA (cafeteria) YTD 0.00 as of 07/15/2025, so all 3,500 of Halvorsen's code W was contributed after the household became Texas residents (residency: TX from 2025-07-15). D09 itself notes payroll wrongly kept CA as the work state (qa-45). For a part-year resident the CA-sourced HSA add-back should be the Corvane 2,500 only; the engine relied on an erroneous box 16. The broader box 16 problem belongs to the wages/California area; this finding covers the HSA component.
findings.expected: CA-sourced HSA add-back 2,500 (contributions during CA residency)
findings.actual: 6,000 added and fully included in the California amount
findings.estimated_tax_effect: About 224 CA overstatement on the HSA component alone (3,500 x 0.064 ca_source_income); no federal effect.
findings.proposed_check: ca_addback_by_residency_period: allocate each W-2 add-back item to CA/non-CA using contribution dates from paystubs vs household.residency; flag when the CA column includes post-move amounts.

findings.title: SEP contribution 18,000 exceeds deductible limit by 2,786; recorded as carryover but never flagged
findings.description: D26 confirms an 18,000 SEP-IRA deposit on 04/10/2026 for 2025 (ev-0485, ev-0486). Sch1.16 deducts 15,214 (R-SEP-LIMIT: 20% x (81,854 - 5,783)), and v3 carryovers_out.federal.sep_contribution_not_deductible_for_2025 = 2,786. No diagnostic warns about the 2,786 nondeductible excess, no return line shows it, and engine_reference has no rule for its treatment. The reviewer must decide how the excess is handled (withdraw by the due date vs carry to 2026) and the client, who said 'we plan to put 18,000' (qa-26), should be told the deduction is limited. Also check that the 20% limit used the correct net profit if the Schedule C area changes SchC.31.
findings.expected: Diagnostic: SEP contribution 18,000 > deductible limit 15,214; excess 2,786 needs a decision
findings.actual: Silent; excess only visible in carryovers_out
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Deduction itself is correct at 15,214; the excess 2,786 is a client decision with possible excise exposure (not in engine_reference).

findings.title: v1 and v2 deducted the SEP based on a stated intention, before any contribution existed

findings.estimated_tax_effect: None in v3; 15,214 x 0.31 = about 4,716 federal exposure if filed unfunded.

findings.title: 2025 Form 5498 arrived 2026-05-29, after the original due date; F8606 lines were client-sourced until v3
findings.description: D43 was received 2026-05-29 (tl-14) and is in documents_used only from v3 (2026-06-23). findings.expected: 5498 for 2025 in file before the 8606 is released
findings.actual: Received 2026-05-29; used from v3
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None (values agree).

findings.title: Prior preparer open item 'Confirm 2024 Form 5498 for IRA basis' is now satisfied by D42
findings.description: D07 p2 says '8606: basis 7,000 per client ... 5498 not obtained' and D07 p3 lists 'Confirm 2024 Form 5498 for IRA basis' as open. findings.title: Full-year Travis County tax 13,420 deducted although seller credited 6,912 for 01/01-07/07 at closing
findings.description: SchA.5b = 13,420 from D57 box 10 / D58 (home bought 07/08/2025; D58 says owner of record 01/01/2025 was the prior owner). D54 buyer closing statement shows 'Seller credit for 2025 county taxes 01/01/2025-07/07/2025: 6,912.00' (ev-1027, 0.99, unused). The buyer's own real estate tax is 13,420 - 6,912 = 6,508. Rule R-SALT-PROPERTY ('real estate taxes paid on the home') has no proration logic. Because SchA.5d (41,290) only exceeds the 40,000 cap by 1,290, this correction drops SALT below the cap: 27,870 + 6,508 = 34,378. California itemized (no cap) also falls by 6,912. Engine applied the analogous proration correctly on the condo SALE (SchE.16B = 5,544 from D51), so the treatment is internally inconsistent.
findings.expected: SchA.5b = 6,508; SchA.5d = 34,378; SchA.5e = 34,378; SchCA540NR.A.itemized reduced by 6,912
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Federal approx. +1,462 (5,622 x 0.26 once under the cap); California approx. +332 (6,912 x 0.048). Requires partner sign-off (>1,000).
findings.proposed_check: property_tax_proration: when a home was acquired during the year and the closing statement has a seller tax credit, SchA.5b must equal taxes paid minus the credit; also flag when a 1098 box 10 / county receipt covers a levy period starting before the purchase date.

Lines: F1040.25a/25d/26/31/33/37/38, Sch3.10/11/15, F2210.8/19/AI, F540NR.71/72/73/78/97, FTB5805.penalty. All three versions carry identical payment lines except Sch3.10 (0 -> 36,000 in v3). engine_reference.parameters: prior_year_tax 37557, prior_year_agi 228409, ca_prior_year_tax 12520, fed/ca underpayment rate 0.07, ss_wage_base 176100. findings.title: Federal Q4 estimated payment taken from client's guess (4,000) instead of IRS transcript (3,000)
findings.description: F1040.26 = 13,000 in v1, v2 and v3 = 9,000 from D67 plus 4,000 from qa-41 ('Paid January 14, 2026 - 4,000 I think'). D67 prints only three confirmations (04/15, 06/16, 09/15, 3,000 each). The IRS account transcript (D69, pulled 2026-03-12, in documents_used for v2 and v3) shows code 670 on 2026-01-15 for 3,000, and the 2026-08-03 snapshot shows the same. The engine kept the client's unverified figure in v2 and v3 even after the transcript was in the file and raised no diagnostic. Total payments should be 76,742 not 77,742; F1040.37 should be 5,220 not 4,220. The what_if.extension estimate and the 36,000 Form 4868 payment were also computed from payments that included the unverified 4,000.
findings.proposed_check: estimates_agree_to_transcript: for each 1040-ES installment, match amount and date across payment confirmation, questionnaire answer and IRS 670 transactions for the same tax period; flag any line value whose only source for a payment is a questionnaire answer when a transcript is on file
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Federal balance due understated by 1,000 (payments change balance 1:1); Form 2210 penalty understated by roughly 17-19

findings.title: California estimated payments include a 3,500 payment the client designated to tax year 2024
findings.description: F540NR.72 = 14,000 sums four 3,500 Web Pay payments. The 2025-09-15 payment is printed on D68 as 'tax year 2024 (estimated payment)' and the pipeline read it correctly (ev-1076 = '2024', conf 0.98), but rule R-CA-ESTIMATED-PAYMENTS selects every FTB payment dated 2025-04-01..2026-01-15 regardless of designation. FTB's account record lists only 10,500 of 2025 payments and shows the 3,500 'held as a 2024 credit'. The 540NR therefore claims 3,500 more in payments than FTB will credit; FTB will reduce the refund (timeline tl-26) and issue a notice unless the credit is transferred to 2025 first. California also requires no third-quarter installment (R-CA-5805: 30/40/0/30), so a 9/15 payment is itself unusual and worth a client question.
findings.proposed_check: ca_payment_year_designation: for every FTB payment, require extracted tax-year field == return year before including it in F540NR.72, and reconcile the resulting total to agency:/ftb_account.tax_year_2025_payments; flag payments held as prior-year credits
findings.estimated_tax_effect: California refund overstated by 3,500 (payments change balance 1:1); no change to tax

findings.title: Form 2210 penalty computed from the unverified 4,000 Q4 payment; should be recomputed
findings.description: F2210.8 = 41,313 is correct (110% x 37,557 = 41,312.70; prior AGI 228,409 > 150,000; 90% x 81,962 = 73,766 is larger). Required installments 10,328; withholding 6,350 per period plus 3,000 estimates leaves 978 underpaid for Q1-Q3; the engine's Q4 of 4,000 on 2026-01-14 covers Q4, giving 164 (recomputed ~165 at 7% to 2026-04-15). With the transcript's 3,000 on 2026-01-15, Q4 is also underpaid by 978 for 90 days (+16.88), so the penalty is roughly 181 (simple per-period) to 183 (cumulative application). F2210.19 cites qa-41 as a source, not the transcript. Note the extension payment on 2026-04-14 does not change the 2210 penalty (the rule accrues only to 2026-04-15). what_if.penalty_annualized confirms the annualized method does not help (annualized installments exceed regular).
findings.expected: F2210.19 approximately 181-183 using Q4 = 3,000 paid 2026-01-15
findings.proposed_check: recompute_2210_regular: independently recompute the regular-method penalty from F1040.24, prior-year tax, withholding and agency-confirmed payment dates/amounts; flag if it differs from F1040.38 by more than 1
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Penalty understated by about 17-19

findings.title: Post-filing interest and failure-to-pay penalty on the federal balance paid 2026-07-20
findings.description: tl-25: balance paid 2026-07-20, 96 days after 2026-04-15. post_filing_rates: interest 7%/yr, FTP 0.5% per month or part (Apr 16-May 15, May 16-Jun 15, Jun 16-Jul 15, Jul 16-20 = 4 months = 2%). On the v3 balance 4,220: interest 77.69, FTP 84.40, total about 162. On the corrected balance 5,220 (finding 1): interest 96.11, FTP 104.40, total about 200. The transcript (as_of 2026-08-03) shows 196/276 'computed by IRS'; the workpaper should pre-compute the expected notice so the client is not surprised. Reviewer should also consider whether the amount paid by 2026-04-15 (76,742-77,742 of 81,962, i.e. 93.6-94.9%) affects the FTP penalty during the extension period; the packet does not state a rule either way.

Records retention is 7 years after filing, so the file must still exist in 2028.

Carryovers_into_2025 (ST 3,200 / LT 11,000 / passive 6,300 + 9,850 / IRA basis 7,000; all other categories 0) equal what the 2024 return computes and land correctly in v3 SchD.6, SchD.14, F8582.1c, F8606.2; no AMT credit, charitable, NOL, 1231 or QBI loss carryovers exist and F4797.8 correctly uses 0. carryovers_out v3: minimum tax credit 3,871 (= F6251.11), SEP excess 2,786, IRA basis 0, S corp basis 0, Ridgeline capital 63,660, CA depreciation basis differences. Variance review (firm rule >10% and >1,000) flags 52 of the 83 comparable lines because of the condo sale, job change, ISO exercise, equipment purchase, itemizing for the first time and late K-1s; the swings that lack a documented explanation are listed as a finding. Dependents: same two children both years; Ada (dob 2006-05-21) was 18 at end of 2024 and 19 as a full-time student in 2025, so ODC 500 both years is consistent; Theo (dob 2017-02-09) CTC both years; 2024 credit 2,500 vs 2025 400 is explained by the 400,000 phase-out. Filing status MFJ both years; address changed Sacramento to Austin consistent with the move. prior_year_agi_for_esignature 228,409 = D06 F1040.11 = ref:param.prior_year_agi (agrees). Engine behaviors of note: R-SCORP-BASIS-ROLLFORWARD assumes no change for unknown years (v1/v2 used 8,200, v3 used 2,300 after D40); R-CA-ESTIMATED-PAYMENTS counts every FTB payment by date and ignores the designated tax year; R-INTEREST-PAYER converted 2025 SEK interest at the 2024 average rate; key-based prior-year comparison is unreliable for Schedule B.

findings.title: Theo's SSN in household differs from 2024 return and SS card; caused e-file rejection
findings.description: household.people[theo].ssn is 666-74-3309, but the 2024 return (D06 page 1, ev-0012) shows 666-74-3390 and the Social Security card (D71, ev-1080) confirms 666-74-3390. The transposition entered in the organizer flowed into v3 (F8812.4 sources household:theo) and the federal return was rejected 2026-07-13 with R0000-504-02 (dependent 2 TIN/name control). msg-10 confirms the organizer typo. A prior-year-to-household comparison of dependent SSNs would have caught this before the client signed Form 8879 on 2026-07-10. California was held (STATE-HOLD) as a consequence.
findings.actual: 666-74-3309 in household (used by v3)
findings.estimated_tax_effect: No tax change; filing validity: federal rejection 2026-07-13, resubmitted and accepted 2026-07-14; CTC 2,200 for Theo depends on a valid SSN.
findings.proposed_check: dependent_identity_vs_prior_year: compare each dependent's name, SSN and DOB in household against the prior-year return's extracted dependent fields (and any identity document); block e-file on mismatch.

findings.title: California 2025-09-15 payment of 3,500 was designated tax year 2024 but v3 counts it as a 2025 estimated payment
findings.description: D68 printed_content and ev-1076 (tax year 2024, confidence 0.98) show the 2025-09-15 Web Pay of 3,500 was designated to tax year 2024, and agency:/ftb_account shows it 'held as a 2024 credit', with only three 2025 payments (3,500 x 3 = 10,500) on the 2025 account. Rule R-CA-ESTIMATED-PAYMENTS counts every FTB payment dated 2025-04-01 to 2026-01-15 regardless of designated year, so F540NR.72 = 14,000. The 2024 CA return (CA540.111 1,240 paid 2025-03-28) was already fully paid, so the 3,500 sits as an unapplied 2024 overpayment. Unless the credit is transferred, FTB will reduce the 8,256 refund by 3,500.
findings.expected: F540NR.72 = 10,500 (payments designated 2025), plus a request to FTB to transfer the 3,500 2024 credit to 2025
findings.estimated_tax_effect: California refund overstated by 3,500 (payments change balance 1:1) until the 2024 credit is moved.
findings.proposed_check: payment_designated_year_vs_agency: for each payment confirmation, compare designated tax year to the return year and to the agency account (FTB/IRS) ledger; flag payments the agency holds in another year.

findings.title: Northlake sweep interest counted twice (composite 1099 and standalone 1099-INT for the same account)
findings.description: D28 page 1 (Northlake Securities consolidated 1099, account ending 7731) includes a 1099-INT 'bank sweep program, Northlake Bank' box 1 1,840.00 (ev-0492). D29 is a standalone 1099-INT from Northlake Bank, N.A. 'bank sweep program for Northlake Securities account ending 7731', box 1 1,840.00 (ev-0538). v3 reports both as separate payers (SchB.1.1 and SchB.1.2, each 1,840). The 2024 return had a single Northlake line (SchB.1.1 bank sweep 1,180) - the payer-level prior-year comparison shows one Northlake payer becoming two with identical amounts. Both reads are correct; the duplication is at the document/engine level.
findings.expected: One Northlake sweep interest line of 1,840; SchB.2 = 4,610
findings.actual: Two lines of 1,840; SchB.2 = 6,450
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Interest overstated 1,840: federal about 640 (0.348/dollar), California about 75 (0.041/dollar); also flows to F8960 NIIT and SchCA540NR.2.
findings.proposed_check: interest_payer_dedupe: flag interest lines with identical amount where one document references the other's account number or payer (composite 1099 vs standalone 1099-INT), and payers that appear once in the prior year but twice now.

findings.title: Federal Q4 estimated payment 4,000 per client vs 3,000 on IRS transcript
findings.description: F1040.26 = 13,000 built from EFTPS confirmations (3 x 3,000, ev-1056..1061) plus the client's questionnaire answer qa-41 ('Paid January 14, 2026 - 4,000 I think') for Q4, since no confirmation was uploaded (rule R-ESTIMATED-PAYMENTS). Both IRS transcript snapshots (2026-03-12 and 2026-08-03) show the 2026-01-15 payment as 3,000. The firm's required step 'Estimated payments agreed to IRS and FTB records' is not met. Prior year F1040.26 was 6,000 (4 x 1,500 pattern suggests even payments).
findings.expected: F1040.26 = 12,000 (IRS transcript)
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Federal balance due understated by 1,000; also changes F2210 penalty slightly.
findings.proposed_check: estimated_payments_vs_transcript: match each claimed estimated payment (date, amount) to IRS transcript code 670 entries; flag any claimed payment without a transcript match, especially those sourced from a questionnaire answer.

findings.title: Sparbanken 2025 interest converted at the 2024 average SEK rate
findings.description: SchB.1.6 label says 'SEK 18,450.00 at 10.56 SEK/USD' and sources ref:fx.SEK.2024_average. engine_reference.parameters.fx.SEK has 2025_average 9.86. The 2024 return (SchB.1.4) correctly used 10.56 for 2024; the engine reused the prior-year rate for 2025. 18,450 / 9.86 = 1,871 vs 1,747 reported. (The Form 8938 values correctly use the 2025 year-end rate 9.71.)
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Interest understated 124: federal about 43, California about 5.
findings.proposed_check: fx_rate_year_matches_tax_year: every foreign-currency conversion on a 2025 line must cite a 2025 rate (average for income, year-end for balances); flag citations of a prior-year rate.

findings.title: Prior preparer open item still unresolved: 2023 Form 3520 for the Swedish inheritance
findings.description: D07 page 3 lists '2023 Form 3520 (foreign inheritance over 100,000) - discussed? (no note of resolution)'. The 2025 packet confirms the facts: qa-07 'inherited from his mother in 2023', D36 'Account opened 09/2023 (inheritance from Birgitta Lindqvist)', balance SEK 1,196,800 at year end and 2024 Form 8938 maximum 151,880 USD. No document, questionnaire answer (qa-08 asks only about 2025), message or call note addresses whether a 2023 Form 3520 was filed. Of the four open items left by the prior preparer, this is the only one not addressed: 2023 Woodworks K-1 (resolved by D40 on 2026-06-05), 2024 Form 5498 (resolved by D42), home office square footage (resolved by D24).
findings.expected: A record that Form 3520 for 2023 was filed, or a decision to file late / disclose
findings.actual: No resolution anywhere in the packet; engine has no diagnostic
findings.estimated_tax_effect: No 2025 tax change; potential penalty exposure on a 2023 information return (outside the engine), reputational risk if ignored again.
findings.proposed_check: prior_open_items_rollforward: carry each prior-preparer open item into the current workpaper as a required-resolution item; block sign-off until each is marked resolved with a reference or explicitly deferred by partner.

findings.title: Client says no prior IRA basis; 2024 Form 8606 and 2024 Form 5498 show 7,000
findings.description: qa-31: 'Prior basis: none that I know of - we started doing this in 2025.' The 2024 return D06 page 10 reports F8606.1/3/14 = 7,000 (ev-2991..2993), D42 shows a 7,000 contribution for 2024 made 02/12/2025, and D07 page 2 notes the backdoor Roth started with the 2024 contribution. v3 F8606.2 = 7,000 (from py:/return_2024/lines/F8606.14 and ev-0991), so the engine followed the documents and the 14,026 conversion is 99.8% nontaxable (F8606.18 = 26). The client's answer is wrong but should be confirmed so the client understands the 14,000 total basis and so no 2024 IRA deduction was taken elsewhere.
findings.expected: Prior basis 7,000 (documents)
findings.actual: Client states none; engine used 7,000
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None if documents are right; if the 2024 basis were not valid, 7,000 more of the conversion would be taxable (about 2,170 federal at 0.31).
findings.proposed_check: questionnaire_vs_prior_return: compare every questionnaire answer that has a prior-year counterpart (IRA basis, carryovers, dependents, foreign accounts) to the prior-year return line and flag contradictions for client confirmation.

findings.title: S corporation basis records not rolled forward after the 2023 K-1 arrived; v1/v2 used an assumed basis
findings.description: basis_records still show 2023 and 2024 ending_stock_basis null. With D40 (2023 K-1: income 14,100, distributions 20,000) the roll is 21,300 + 14,100 - 20,000 = 15,400 (2023) and 15,400 + 16,900 - 30,000 = 2,300 (2024), which is what v3 F7203.1 uses. v1 and v2 used 8,200 (rule R-SCORP-BASIS-ROLLFORWARD assumed no 2023 change), so the extension estimate (36,000 paid 2026-04-14 from v2) understated the excess-distribution gain by 5,900 (F7203.excess 15,315 -> 21,215; F8949.F.SCORP). The prior preparer's 'assumed basis sufficient' for 2024 is now verified (32,300 available vs 30,000 distributed) but only barely; 2025 distributions 42,000 (ev-0977) exceed basis by 21,215.
findings.actual: basis_records null/null; v3 F7203.1 = 2,300 (correct), v1/v2 = 8,200
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Already in v3 (5,900 x 0.238 = about 1,404 federal more than v2); records housekeeping only.
findings.proposed_check: basis_rollforward_complete: recompute S corp stock basis year by year from stored K-1 figures and flag any year with null ending basis once the K-1 for that year is in file; compare to F7203.1.

findings.title: California passive carryovers equal federal although the prior preparer notes a CA depreciation difference; 2024 CA return made no depreciation adjustment
findings.description: py:/carryovers_into_2025/california gives passive_1450_fremont 6,300 and 1200_barton_hills 9,850 - identical to federal - while its note says CA differs because SAC-APPL has remaining California basis (federal took 100% bonus in 2021; CA 200DB: 840 / 1,344 / 806.40 / 483.84 in 2021-2024). The 2024 CA return (D06 page 12) shows only the HSA addition of 2,400 on Schedule CA and no rental depreciation adjustment, so the CA suspended loss for Fremont Way was never tracked separately from federal. v3 SchE.22A sources py:/carryovers_into_2025/passive_1450_fremont for both jurisdictions and only adjusts 2025 depreciation (SchCA540NR.17.B 484). Which CA carryover is right needs a reviewer decision (cumulative CA-vs-federal depreciation on SAC-APPL: 2021 CA lower by 3,360; 2022-2024 CA higher by 2,634).
findings.expected: A CA-specific suspended loss for Fremont Way that reflects CA depreciation, or a documented conclusion that it equals federal
findings.actual: CA carryover = federal (6,300) with a note saying it should differ; no 2024 Schedule CA depreciation adjustment
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Small: at most a few hundred dollars of California-source loss (ca_source_income 0.063/dollar) for 2025; all passive losses are released in 2025 so the amount matters this year.
findings.proposed_check: state_carryover_vs_federal_with_basis_difference: where asset records show state/federal depreciation differences for an activity, require state carryovers to differ from federal by the cumulative difference (or a documented reason); flag identical values.

findings.title: 2024 home office used 300 sq ft; client's measurement of the same Sacramento room is 220 sq ft
findings.description: D07 page 2 flagged 'Home office 300 sq ft (Sacramento rental house, 2 rooms combined?) - client to confirm' and left it open. D24 (ev-0481) gives the Sacramento studio as 11 x 20 = 220 sq ft. The 2024 SchC.30 deduction of 1,500 (ev-2953) was therefore overstated by 400. For 2025 the engine averaged 240 sq ft (SchC.30 = 1,200; exact monthly average 220 x 6.5 + 260 x 5.5 over 12 = 238, i.e. 1,192). Engine diagnostic HOME_OFFICE_AREA_CHANGE notes the change but not that the prior year was wrong.
findings.estimated_tax_effect: 2025: about 10 of deduction (3 federal). 2024: 400 overstated (about 120 federal in 2024) - not worth amending; note for the file.
findings.proposed_check: prior_open_item_resolution_backtests_prior_year: when a prior open item is resolved with a figure that differs from what the prior return used, flag the prior-year line as potentially misstated and record the decision.

findings.title: Prior-year variance review: swings over 10% and 1,000 without a documented explanation
findings.description: Applying firm variance_review to the 83 same-key lines flags 52. Most are explained in the packet: wages +56,361 (job change, two W-2s, RSU/ESPP; qa-03, qa-06), capital gain -3,000 -> 185,027 (condo sale D51/D52, 282 brokerage sales, S corp excess distributions, crypto), adjustments 5,080 -> 35,397 (SEP D26, SEHI D25), itemized 85,706 vs standard 29,200 (home purchase D54/D55/D57, charity D63-D66), SchC.13 depreciation 38,000 (equipment D22, qa-18), SchE.14A repairs 3,900 -> 13,300 (HVAC 11,000, qa-37; what_if hvac_improvement shows 3,633 federal if treated as improvement), property B lines (sold 10/15, 9.5 months), CTC 2,500 -> 400 (phase-out), QBI 16,744 -> 12,971 (wage/UBIA limit), F8582.4 (passive income released by the sale), F2441.2 6,200 -> 9,600 (two centers after the move). Swings with NO explanation in the packet: (1) F1040.25a withholding 31,950 -> 25,400 (-20%) while wages rose 36% (box 2: D08 ev-0017 15,800 + D09 ev-0036 9,600) - ask whether a W-2 box 2 is misread or withholding was changed; (2) SchC.44a business miles 7,400 -> 11,800 (+59%) and SchC.9 4,958 -> 8,260, from a handwritten log (D23) - ask client why; (3) SchC.11 contract labor 12,400 -> 7,400 (-40%) and SchC.24a travel 6,100 -> 4,520 (-26%); (4) Sparbanken interest SEK 3,700 -> 18,450 (5x) on a balance that fell from a 2024 max of ~151,880 USD; (5) SchB Northlake 1,180 -> 3,680 across two lines (see duplicate finding); (6) SchE.3A rents +600 but management fee only +48 (8% of 37,200 = 2,976 is consistent, fine). Taxable interest 2,310 -> 6,450 (+179%) is explained only if the Northlake duplicate and FX issues are fixed (then 4,734).
findings.expected: Every flagged swing carries an explanation reference (document, questionnaire answer or rule)
findings.actual: 52 flagged lines; at least 5 swings have no explanation in the packet
findings.estimated_tax_effect: Unknown until explained; withholding alone is a 6,550 swing in payments.
findings.proposed_check: variance_review_with_explanations: compute change vs prior year per comparable line (matching Schedule B/E lines by payer/property, not key position), flag >10% and >1,000, and require an explanation tag (event: move, job change, sale, new document) before reviewer sign-off.

findings.title: Self-employed health insurance deduction claimed although client confirms Erik was eligible for Ngozi's employer plan
findings.description: The 2024 return took no SEHI deduction with the note 'Erik was covered on Ngozi's employer plan in 2024'. For 2025 v3 Sch1.17 = 14,400 (D25 individual plan). qa-25 says both of Ngozi's 2025 employers offered family coverage and Erik kept his own plan by choice. Rule R-SEHI only limits the deduction to business income less half SE tax and SEP; it does not test eligibility for employer-subsidized coverage. This is a prior-year-informed judgment call for the reviewer; the engine produced no diagnostic.
findings.expected: Reviewer decision on eligibility months recorded with authority
findings.actual: Full-year 14,400 deducted with no eligibility review
findings.estimated_tax_effect: If disallowed: about 4,464 federal (14,400 x 0.31, plus QBI interplay) and about 619 California (0.043).
findings.proposed_check: sehi_eligibility_gate: when a prior-year note or questionnaire indicates employer coverage eligibility, require a month-by-month eligibility confirmation before allowing Sch1.17.

findings.title: Schedule B line keys are positional; same-key prior-year comparison misattributes payers
findings.description: 2024 SchB.1.2 is Meridian U.S. Treasury interest (560) while v3 SchB.1.2 is Northlake Bank (1,840); 2024 SchB.1.3 is Sacramento Valley Bank, v3 SchB.1.3 is Meridian; 2024 SchB.1.4 is Sparbanken, v3 SchB.1.4 is Austin Community Credit Union. A key-based variance report would flag the wrong lines and miss the real payer-level changes (Sparbanken 350 -> 1,747; Sacramento Valley Bank 220 -> 96). Schedule E property columns (A/B) and F8949 lots have the same problem in principle.
findings.expected: Comparison by payer name / property address / asset id
findings.actual: Only positional keys available
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None directly; affects detection quality.
findings.proposed_check: payer_matched_prior_year_compare: normalize payer names (and EIN/account where extracted) and match Schedule B/E lines across years by entity, reporting added, removed and changed payers.

findings.title: Form 2441 provider name differs from the provider statement and the 2024 return

findings.expected: Bright Oak Kids Club, 68-0412257
findings.actual: Bright Oak Preschool, 68-0412257
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None (credit is 0 after the 5,000 exclusion).
findings.proposed_check: provider_name_vs_statement_and_prior_year: compare Form 2441 provider name/EIN to the provider statement text and to the prior-year Form 2441 entry with the same EIN.

findings.title: Ridgeline K-1 arrived after the extension; outside basis still never computed
findings.description: The 2024 return reported Ridgeline (K1_1065 box 2 7,900, ending capital 60,000). v1 and v2 carried diagnostic K1_EXPECTED_NOT_RECEIVED; D37/D38 were received 2026-06-22 (qa-13 and msg-01 predicted June) and first used in v3, adding 8,400 rental income, 120 interest, 1,350 LTCG and 210 foreign tax (Sch3.1 186 -> 396). The capital account rolls correctly (60,000 + 9,870 - 6,000 - 210 = 63,660, ev-0969/ev-0970, carryovers_out.ridgeline_capital_account_end). basis_records.partnership_ridgeline still records outside_basis null ('never computed'); distributions 6,000 are well below capital so no gain issue, but the gap persists for next year.
findings.expected: Outside basis computed (at least capital account 63,660 as a proxy) and stored for 2026 roll-forward
findings.actual: outside_basis null; capital account 63,660 carried out
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None for 2025.
findings.proposed_check: k1_expected_from_prior_year: list every pass-through entity on the prior-year return, track receipt date vs extension/filing dates, and require a basis figure (stock or outside) stored for each entity at year end.

findings.title: 2023 return not in the file although three prior-year threads depend on it
findings.description: The packet holds the 2024 return (D06), the 2024 workpaper (D07) and a 2023 CP2000 (D70) but not the 2023 Form 1040. It is needed to (a) verify the 2024 F8582.1c prior-year unallowed losses of 8,555 (A) and 4,976 (B) that feed the 6,300 / 9,850 carryovers, (b) confirm the 2023 Woodworks K-1 income 14,100 (D40) was reported in 2023 (the CP2000 concerned only a 1099-B), and (c) check whether the 2023 Form 3520 was filed. The firm's required step 'Prior-year return reviewed' covers only 2024.
findings.expected: 2023 return (or transcript) on file
findings.actual: Not in packet
findings.estimated_tax_effect: None directly.
findings.proposed_check: prior_year_chain_completeness: when a carryover or open item originates before the immediately prior year, require that year's return or transcript to be on file.

open_questions.question: Was a Form 3520 filed for 2023 for the inheritance from Birgitta Lindqvist (the Sparbanken account opened 09/2023, about 150,000 USD)? If not, do you have the inheritance documents and date so we can advise on a late filing?

Your 2024 return shows a 7,000 nondeductible IRA contribution for 2024 made on 2025-02-12 (Form 8606 basis 7,000), but the organizer says there was no prior basis. Please confirm the 2024 contribution and that no IRA deduction was taken for it.
Please upload the EFTPS confirmation for the January 2026 federal estimated payment; the IRS transcript shows 3,000, not 4,000.

area: Engine integrity (v1/v2/v3 return_versions): arithmetic, source-to-line agreement, summaries, change logs, document usage, parameters, diagnostics, data model
area_notes: Three engine runs: v1 2026-03-04 (625 lines), v2 2026-03-19 (625 lines; D31 corrected Meridian 1099 replaces D30, D69 transcript added), v3 2026-06-23 (627 lines; adds D26, D37, D38, D40, D43, D73; SchB.1.8 and SchE.28B added). No document is used before its received_at; D30 is the only received-but-unused doc in v2/v3 (superseded) and no D30 ev id is cited in v2/v3. 15 documents in v3 documents_used cite no ev at all: D01-D07, D10, D13, D15, D47, D54, D69, D70, D73 (D69 and D70 are not_extracted; D73 paystub and D54 buyer closing statement carry figures the engine needed but ignored). All summary totals equal their lines in every version (F1040.11/15/24/33/37/38; F540NR.17/32/64/78/97; FTB5805). changes_from_previous is complete and accurate for v1->v2 and v2->v3 (every changed/added line listed with correct old/new; nothing listed that did not change). All diagnostics refs resolve. what_if: every alternative's base equals v3 summary and total_tax_change = alternative - base; california blocks omit penalty_change. Data model (v3): 627 lines across 34 (jurisdiction, form) groups: federal F1040 31, Sch1 8, Sch2 6, Sch3 5, SchA 13, SchB 16, SchC 26, SchD 16, SchE 29, SchSE 7, F2210 3, F2441 6, F4562-C 4, F4562-E 2, F4797 11, F6251 11, F7203 9, F8283 2, F8582 5, F8606 14, F8812 8, F8863 3, F8867 1, F8889 6, F8938 3, F8949 302 (260 Brightpath X lots, 17 Meridian M lots, 5 Northlake N lots, 12 Coinhaven C lots, 1 S-corp excess-distribution lot, 7 box totals), F8959 7, F8960 9, F8995 9; california SchCA540NR 30 (keys <line>.<column A-E>), F540NR 19, FTB3885A 4, FTB5805 1, ScheduleS 1. 95 distinct rule ids. Value types: int 316, float 298 (F8949 lots in cents plus three ratios F8606.10, F540NR.34, F540NR.36), str 13 (Yes/No flags, dates, property descriptions, 'days / personal' strings, 'Not completed'). Source prefixes in v3: ev 1,956 citations (1,914 distinct ev ids, 1,560 from D74), asset 18, ref:param/fx 13, py: 12, qa 9, household 6, timeline 1. 11 California lines take federal line keys as inputs (SchCA540NR.*.A columns, SchCA540NR.26.D, SchCA540NR.A.itemized, F540NR.13, F540NR.61). 5 lines have neither inputs nor sources (SchB.8, F4797.26g, SchD.18, F8960.14=250000 hard-coded, F540NR.73=0). R-SUM carries no sign metadata: 20+ R-SUM lines are differences (SchC.29/31, SchE.21A/B, F1040.11/15/22/37, F6251.6/9/10/11, F8812.12, F540NR.17/19/32/40/64/97), so a recomputation layer needs per-line sign conventions. Several lines list inputs they do not use (F8582.1a lists SchE.21B; SchCA540NR.12.A lists F1040.8). tax_effect_rates are stated per version; federal rates are explainable (taxpayer is in AMT: 26% + 5% CTC phase-out = 0.31 wages; +3.8% NIIT = 0.348 investment; 0.238 LTCG) but California rates move a lot between versions with no structural change.
